```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(palmerpenguins)
```

## What is broom and how is it used? {transition="slide"}

::: incremental
- broom is an R package that helps convert the outputs of statistical objects into tidy tibbles
- broom is especially useful for comparing models, visualizing outputs, building organized reports, or analyzing model fits
- broom is part of the tidyverse ecosystem (installed with tidyverse), but you will need to load either tidymodels or broom itself to use it
:::

## Methods {transition="slide" auto-animate=true}

::: incremental
- tidy() - summarize model components
- glance() - report model-level information
- augment() - add information about each observation
:::

## Messy model outputs {transition="slide" auto-animate=true}

```{r}
#| echo: true
lm1 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins)
summary(lm1)
```

## Using broom to summarize model components {transition="slide" auto-animate=true}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "2"
lm1 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins)
tidy(lm1)
```

## Using broom to report model information (and compare models!) {transition="slide" auto-animate=true}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "4"
lm1 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins)
lm2 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm + species, data = penguins) 

models_df <- rbind(glance(lm1), glance(lm2))

lrt <- 2 * (models_df$logLik[2] - models_df$logLik[1])
lrt
```

## Using broom to add information to each observation {transition="slide" auto-animate=true}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1"
#| output-location: slide
augment(lm1) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "Red") +
  labs(
    x = "Fitted Values",
    y = "Residuals",
    title = "Residual Plot for Linear Regression"
  )
```
